title: Clear NFT Metadata Keeps the Complete Domain Name Visible

cover.subtitle: Preserve readable names and verifiable identifiers.
cover.visual: One small NFT display card labeled example.com, beside a tiny metadata document icon. No invented verification seal.

sections.name: 01-the-domain-label-and-the-token-identity-serve-different-jobs
sections.heading: The domain label and the token identity serve different jobs
sections.scene: A readable example.com card sits beside chain, contract, and token-ID identifiers. The full suffix remains visible, with name and identity shown as distinct fields.
sections.alt: The domain label and the token identity serve different jobs.

sections.name: 02-metadata-connects-the-readable-label-to-the-displayed-asset
sections.heading: Metadata connects the readable label to the displayed asset
sections.scene: A tokenURI arrow leads to JSON name/image/external_url fields, then to an NFT card and asset inspection page. No third-party logos.
sections.alt: Metadata connects the readable label to the displayed asset.

sections.name: 03-a-consistent-image-layout-keeps-complete-names-readable
sections.heading: A consistent image layout keeps complete names readable
sections.scene: Four equal-sized generic token thumbnail cards show typography tests. Only readable labels Short, Long, Hyphenated, Internationalized. A separate magnifier highlights a complete example.com label. No other domain strings, no verification badges.
sections.alt: A consistent image layout keeps complete names readable.

sections.name: 04-display-updates-need-verification-across-separate-caches
sections.heading: Display updates need verification across separate caches
sections.scene: Four separate boxes show current tokenURI, metadata JSON, image file, and marketplace cache. A metadata update event triggers refresh arrows without instant-update claims.
sections.alt: Display updates need verification across separate caches.

purpose: Initial illustration plan. The final image review manifest records actual asset hashes and visual revisions.
